title: dedicated-autoscaler-expose-per-fleet-burst-controls-and-improve-util-reporting
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets need finer-grained burst controls and clearer utilization signals to support throughput guarantees and predictable billing. This PR exposes per-fleet burst configuration, smooths token-bucket behavior during rapid scale events, and improves utilization reporting to reduce alert noise and make capacity decisions more actionable.

What changed: added per-fleet burst control APIs, implemented smoothing for the token-bucket refill and drain paths, added additional telemetry (per-fleet request/queued/served histograms), and improved the fleet utilization reporting pipeline to surface transient backpressure events and auto-aggregated 1m/5m/1h utilization windows. Includes end-to-end tests and updated docs.

Checklist:
- [x] API and config schema for per-fleet burst controls
- [x] Autoscaler logic changes (smoother token-bucket, backpressure detection)
- [x] Telemetry + reporting changes + migrating dashboards
- [x] Unit + integration + perf tests
- [x] Docs and release notes

Related: Linear ENG-2013 (fleet burst controls), ENG-2029 (utilization reporting), SUP-4421 (customer incident notes referenced). See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2013/design-dedicated-fleet-burst-controls. References earlier PRs: #412999 (tokenbucket smoothing fix), #370100 (slo-adjustment fixes).

Notes: This is backward-compatible at the config level (new per-fleet block). Default behavior preserves current global token-bucket behavior unless a fleet-specific config is provided. The smoothing introduces a small amortized latency delta in extreme tail cases; perf tests indicate median latency unchanged and P99 within SLA for affected workloads.
author: Marcus Boyd
release_notes: Expose per-fleet burst controls (opt-in), smoother token-bucket behavior to reduce transient backpressure, enhanced fleet utilization reporting with 1m/5m/1h aggregation windows and new telemetry fields.
commits: feat(autoscaler): add per-fleet burst control schema and API
fix(tokenbucket): smoother refill/drain to avoid sharp drops on scale events
test(autoscaler): add integration tests for burst ramp-up/down
docs(dedicated): update autoscaler config guide and examples
patch_snippets: + struct FleetBurstConfig { max_burst_tokens: u64, refill_rate_tokens_per_sec: f64, smoothing_window_secs: u64 }
+ // tokenbucket: apply exponential moving average to refill rate when scale events detected
review_comments: Priya Nair: Can we make the smoothing_window configurable per-fleet? I worry about different workload profiles.
Author (Marcus Boyd): Agreed - added smoothing_window_secs to the config and defaulted to 30s. Updated tests to cover both 10s and 60s windows.
Diego Alvarez: Telemetry looks good. Would like a note about cardinality impact - did we aggregate at the pipeline?
Author (Marcus Boyd): Aggregation is done at the pipeline stage and we emit both raw and rollup metrics; added dashboard notes to docs.
ci_checks: e2e/perf: pass (P95 token throughput within 1.5% of baseline)
